sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Telecommunications Security Code of Practice 2026 (version 1.1): change log
facts: The change log documents updates associated with the 2026 code publication.
It retains the code's risk-based security context.
limits: A change log is lineage evidence rather than operational assurance.
It must be read with the applicable code version.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Explanatory memorandum to the revised Telecommunications Security Code of Practice 2026
facts: The memorandum explains the purpose and expected benefits of the revised code.
It links clearer security duties to resilience of critical telecommunications infrastructure.
limits: An explanatory memorandum is not a compliance decision.
Expected benefits are not measured outcomes.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations and Telecommunications Security Code of Practice
sources.geo: United Kingdom public telecoms networks and services
facts: The publication links the 2022 Security Measures Regulations and the code of practice.
The measures address security risks to public telecoms networks and services.
limits: The publication is a legal-framework landing page.
It does not determine whether a provider is compliant.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Ofcom security report for the period October 2024 to October 2025
facts: The report covers Ofcom's telecoms-security oversight from October 2024 to October 2025.
The publication references proposals to update the 2022 security code.
limits: The landing page does not expose all report details.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Global Coalition on Telecoms: Security and Resilience Principles for 6G
sources.geo: International coalition including the United Kingdom
facts: Seven governments launched 6G security and resilience principles in March 2026.
The initiative was supported by industry partners.
limits: They do not describe current 6G deployment or availability.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: GCOT Security and Resilience Principles for 6G
sources.geo: International coalition including the United Kingdom
facts: The page provides the detailed GCOT principles for future 6G security and resilience.
The publication is available under the Open Government Licence where stated.
limits: The principles are not binding evidence of operator controls.
They do not prove current network service.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.title: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: April 2026 to June 2026
facts: The announcement covers BDUK-subsidised gigabit coverage for April to June 2026.
It describes planned breakdowns of premises receiving coverage as a result of subsidy.
limits: An announcement is not the final statistics release.
Subsidy-attributed coverage is not live retail orderability.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.title: May 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.kind: monthly Project Gigabit contract management information
facts: The page publishes contract-level premises contracted and built for May 2026.
BDUK identifies the release as management information.
limits: Management information is not the same as official statistics.
Built contract counts do not prove a retail service is orderable.
sources.licence: Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated

sources.title: April 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.kind: monthly Project Gigabit contract management information
facts: The page publishes contract-level premises contracted and built for April 2026.
The release is part of BDUK's monthly management-information series.
limits: Monthly figures are a dated snapshot.
Contract delivery counts cannot be assigned directly to parcels.
